rule: choose-chose-chosen (irregular).

rule: Last sprint terminó: Past Simple.
prompt: We ___ three critical bugs last sprint.  (found / have found)

rule: Since + punto de inicio que llega hasta hoy: Present Perfect.
prompt: I ___ in QA since 2019.  (have worked / worked / work)

rule: Período con principio y fin en el pasado: Past Simple.
prompt: I ___ in QA from 2015 to 2019, then I switched to development.  (worked / have worked)

rule: When pregunta por un momento concreto: Past Simple.

rule: Con una fecha (in 2021) va Past Simple.

wrong: I have joined the company in 2021.

rule: Acción en progreso interrumpida: was/were + -ing.

rule: Negativa: wasn't / weren't + -ing.

rule: En progreso en un momento exacto del pasado: were + -ing.

rule: La acción larga de fondo va en Past Continuous.

rule: Contexto de fondo de una historia: Past Continuous.
prompt: I ___ on a fintech app when I first used Cypress.  (was working / worked)

rule: Antes de otro pasado (when I joined): had + participio.
prompt: When I joined, the company ___ (never / use) any automation framework.

rule: La causa ocurrió antes del fallo: Past Perfect.
prompt: The release failed because someone ___ (change) the config manually.
model: The release failed because someone had changed the config manually.

rule: By the time + pasado: had already + participio.

rule: Sin otro pasado de referencia alcanza con Past Simple.

rule: Cantidad o resultado: Present Perfect.

rule: Duración o proceso: Present Perfect Continuous.

rule: Duración antes de otro pasado: had been + -ing.

rule: Venía haciéndolo hasta otro momento pasado: had been + -ing.

model: I had been working as a manual tester for two years when I moved to automation.

rule: En progreso en un momento futuro: will be + -ing.

rule: Pregunta amable sobre planes: Will + sujeto + be + -ing.

q: Say it with used to, you don't do it anymore: I ran the regression manually.
model: I used to run the regression manually.
need_msg: Used to + verbo base: used to run (no used to ran).

q: What time does your daily stand-up start?
model: Our daily stand-up starts at nine thirty.

q: How long does your regression suite take?
model: The full regression suite takes about forty minutes.

q: Who writes the acceptance criteria in your team?
model: The product owner writes the acceptance criteria.

q: How do you report a bug?
model: I write a ticket in Jira with the steps, the expected result and a screenshot.

q: What does your framework do when a test fails?
model: It takes a screenshot and attaches it to the report.

q: Which browsers do you support?
model: We support Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge.

q: How often do you update your test data?
model: We update the test data once a week.

q: What do you like most about QA?
model: I like finding problems before our users do.

q: Where does your team keep the test cases?
model: We keep the test cases in Xray, inside Jira.

q: Say it about the pipeline: I run on every merge.
model: The pipeline runs on every merge.
need_msg: Con un sujeto singular (the pipeline) va -s: runs.

q: Make it a question: She writes the API tests.
model: Does she write the API tests?
need_msg: Pregunta con he/she: Does + sujeto + verbo base (Does she write).

q: Make it negative: Our team works on weekends.
model: Our team doesn't work on weekends.
need_msg: Negativa con un sujeto singular: doesn't + verbo base (doesn't work).

q: What is your team testing this sprint?
model: This sprint we're testing the new payment gateway.

q: Which course are you taking right now?
model: Right now I'm taking a course on Playwright with TypeScript.

q: Why is the staging environment so slow today?
model: It's slow because the team is running load tests on it.

q: What are you reading these days?
model: These days I'm reading a book about software testing.

q: What technology is your company adopting this year?
model: This year my company is adopting AI agents for test generation.

q: Who are you pairing with this week?
model: This week I'm pairing with a backend developer.

q: What are you improving in your test suite at the moment?
model: At the moment I'm improving the reports of the test suite.

q: Say it in Present Continuous, it's happening now: The build fails.
model: The build is failing right now.
need_msg: Sujeto singular + is + -ing: the build is failing.

q: Make it a question in Present Continuous: You work on the login bug.
model: Are you working on the login bug?
need_msg: Pregunta en continuo: Are + sujeto + -ing (Are you working).

q: Make it negative, right now: We deploy to production.
model: We aren't deploying to production right now.
need_msg: Negativa en continuo: aren't + -ing (we aren't deploying).

q: What was your first job in tech?
model: My first job in tech was in a support team.

q: What did you learn in your last project?
model: In my last project I learned a lot about API contracts.

q: How did you find your current job?
model: I found my current job on LinkedIn.

q: When did you write your first automated test?
model: I wrote my first automated test in 2020.

q: What did the developers say about your last bug report?
model: They said the report was very clear.

q: Why did you leave your previous company?
model: I left because I wanted to grow in test automation.

q: What was the hardest bug you fixed last month?
model: Last month I fixed a race condition in the checkout flow.

q: How long did the last release take?
model: The last release took almost three hours.

q: Did you attend the sprint review yesterday?
model: Yes, I attended it and I showed the new test dashboard.

q: What did your team decide in the last retrospective?
model: We decided to run the smoke tests before every merge.

q: Where did you study programming?
model: I studied programming online and in a bootcamp.

q: Say it in Past Simple, with last week: I teach the new tester our framework.
model: Last week I taught the new tester our framework.
need_msg: Teach es irregular: teach, taught, taught.

q: Say it in Past Simple, with yesterday: We buy a new device for mobile testing.
model: Yesterday we bought a new device for mobile testing.
need_msg: Buy es irregular: buy, bought, bought.

q: Say it in Past Simple: The new commit breaks the login page.
model: The new commit broke the login page.
need_msg: Break es irregular: break, broke, broken.

q: Make it a question: The tests passed.
model: Did the tests pass?
need_msg: Pregunta en pasado: Did + sujeto + verbo base (Did the tests pass).

q: Make it negative: I sent the report.
model: I didn't send the report.
need_msg: Negativa en pasado: didn't + verbo base (didn't send).

q: Have you ever led a QA team?
model: Yes, I've led a small QA team of three people.

q: How many bugs have you reported this week?
model: I've reported five bugs this week.

q: Have you finished the test plan yet?
model: Yes, I've already finished the test plan.

q: Which programming languages have you used at work?
model: I've used Java, Python and TypeScript at work.

q: Have you ever worked with a remote team?
model: Yes, I've worked with remote teams in three countries.

q: What has changed in your team since you joined?
model: Since I joined, we've automated most of the regression.

q: Have you ever broken production?
model: Yes, I've broken production once, and I learned a lot from it.

q: Has your company started using AI tools?
model: Yes, my company has started using AI tools for code reviews.

q: How many certifications have you got?
model: I've got two certifications, ISTQB and one in AWS.

q: Have you read the new requirements yet?
model: No, I haven't read them yet.

q: What is the most interesting tool you have tried this year?
model: This year I've tried an AI agent that writes test cases.

q: Say it in Present Perfect, with yet: We didn't find the cause.
model: We haven't found the cause yet.
need_msg: Negativa en Present Perfect: haven't + participio (found), y yet al final.

q: Say it in Present Perfect: She writes the release notes. They're ready now.
model: She has written the release notes.
need_msg: Con she va has, y write tiene participio irregular: has written.

q: Say it in Present Perfect, with already: I tell the developers.
model: I've already told the developers.
need_msg: Already entre have y el participio; tell es irregular: told.

q: Ask about experience, in Present Perfect: Do you use Docker?
model: Have you ever used Docker?
need_msg: Experiencia: Have you ever + participio (used)?

q: Say it in Present Perfect, with just: The pipeline goes green.
model: The pipeline has just gone green.
need_msg: Go es irregular: go, went, gone. Va has just gone.

q: How long have you been using Playwright?
model: I've been using Playwright for two years.
need_msg: Duración: for + cantidad o since + inicio.

q: What have you been working on lately?
model: Lately I've been working on our API test suite.

q: How long has your team been running tests in the cloud?
model: We've been running tests in the cloud since last year.
need_msg: Duración: since last year / for a year.

q: Why are your eyes so red?
model: I've been looking at logs all afternoon.

q: How long have you been waiting for the new environment?
model: I've been waiting for it since Monday.
need_msg: Duración: since Monday / for three days.

q: Say it with for: I started learning Python three months ago, and I'm still learning.
model: I've been learning Python for three months.
need_msg: Con una cantidad de tiempo va for: for three months.

q: Say it in Present Perfect Continuous: The API returns errors since this morning.
model: The API has been returning errors since this morning.
need_msg: Con un sujeto singular: has been + -ing (has been returning).

q: Ask it in Present Perfect Continuous: How long do you work here?
model: How long have you been working here?
need_msg: How long + have you been working...? (no How long do you work).

q: What were you doing when your manager called you?
model: I was reviewing a pull request when my manager called me.

q: What was happening when the server went down?
model: We were running the nightly tests when the server went down.

q: What were you studying when you got your first QA job?
model: I was studying systems engineering when I got my first QA job.

q: Who were you talking to when the build broke?
model: I was talking to the tech lead when the build broke.

q: What was the team doing at five pm yesterday?
model: At five pm yesterday the team was preparing the release.

q: What were you working on before lunch?
model: Before lunch I was working on the flaky login test.

q: Join them with when: I tested the app. It crashed.
model: I was testing the app when it crashed.
need_msg: Acción de fondo en Past Continuous + when + acción corta en Past Simple.

q: Say it in Past Continuous: At midnight we deployed the hotfix.
model: At midnight we were deploying the hotfix.
need_msg: Con we: were + -ing (we were deploying).

q: Had you heard of Playwright before you joined this team?
model: No, I had never heard of Playwright before I joined.

q: What had happened before you arrived at the office?
model: When I arrived, the nightly build had already failed.

q: Why was the client angry?
model: The client was angry because we had missed the deadline.

q: Join them with before: The developers fixed the bug. Then I tested it.
model: The developers had fixed the bug before I tested it.
need_msg: Lo que pasó primero va en Past Perfect: had fixed... before I tested.

q: Join them with when: The meeting finished. Then I arrived.
model: When I arrived, the meeting had already finished.
need_msg: Lo anterior va con had + participio: had already finished.

q: Say it in Past Perfect, with never: Before this job, I didn't use Jira.
model: Before this job, I had never used Jira.
need_msg: Never entre had y el participio: had never used.

q: How long had the test been failing when you noticed it?
model: It had been failing for three days when I noticed it.

q: What had you been doing before you got the alert?
model: I had been reviewing test results before I got the alert.

q: Say it in Past Perfect Continuous: We waited for two hours. Then the build finished.
model: We had been waiting for two hours when the build finished.
need_msg: Duración antes de otro pasado: had been + -ing (had been waiting).

q: The login test is failing. Who will check it?
model: I'll check it right after this meeting.

q: Do you think the release will be on time?
model: I think it will be on time if we fix the blockers today.

q: What will you say if the client asks for a demo?
model: I'll say yes and prepare a short demo.

q: How will AI change QA in five years?
model: I think AI will write most of the basic test cases.

q: Can you help me with this flaky test?
model: Sure, I'll take a look at it now.

q: Make it negative, it's a promise: This change affects the existing tests.
model: This change won't affect the existing tests.
need_msg: Negativa con will: won't + verbo base (won't affect).

q: Say it with when, it's the future: The build will finish, and I'll deploy.
model: When the build finishes, I'll deploy.
need_msg: Después de when con sentido futuro va presente: when the build finishes.

q: What are you going to automate next sprint?
model: Next sprint I'm going to automate the refund flow.

q: What is your company going to launch this year?
model: This year my company is going to launch a new mobile app.

q: Where are you going to work in two years?
model: In two years I'm going to work as an AI QA engineer.

q: The sky is black. What's going to happen?
model: It's going to rain soon.

q: Make it a question with going to: You test the mobile flows.
model: Are you going to test the mobile flows?
need_msg: Pregunta con going to: Are you going to + verbo base?

q: Make it negative with going to: We migrate the tests this year.
model: We aren't going to migrate the tests this year.
need_msg: Negativa: aren't going to + verbo base.

q: Say it in Future Continuous: At three pm I interview a candidate.
model: At three pm I'll be interviewing a candidate.
need_msg: Algo en curso en un momento del futuro: will be + -ing.

q: Will you be using the staging environment this afternoon?
model: Yes, I'll be using it for the regression tests.

q: How many test cases will you have automated by December?
model: By December I'll have automated about five hundred test cases.

q: Say it in Future Perfect, with by Monday: I finish the report.
model: By Monday I'll have finished the report.
need_msg: Terminado antes de un momento del futuro: will have + participio.

q: What tools did you use to work with before Playwright?
model: I used to work with Selenium before Playwright.

q: How did you use to deploy before you had CI?
model: We used to deploy manually every Friday night.

q: Say it with used to, it's not true anymore: I am a manual tester.
model: I used to be a manual tester.
need_msg: Un estado del pasado que ya no es así: used to be.

q: Make it negative with used to: We had code reviews.
model: We didn't use to have code reviews.

rule: El sujeto es obligatorio en inglés, aunque sea it.
prompt: Represents the time that passes.
model: It represents the time that passes.
wrong: Represents the time that passes.

rule: El sujeto es obligatorio: It fails...
prompt: Fails on Safari but works on Chrome.
model: It fails on Safari but works on Chrome.
wrong: Fails on Safari but works on Chrome.

rule: Sujeto obligatorio (it). Y important to me suena más natural.
prompt: Is very important for me.
model: It's very important to me.
wrong: Is very important for me.

rule: Para decir que algo existe: there is / there are.
prompt: Have two critical bugs in staging.
model: There are two critical bugs in staging.
wrong: Have two critical bugs in staging.

rule: El sujeto es obligatorio: It was...
prompt: Was a really hard sprint.
model: It was a really hard sprint.
wrong: Was a really hard sprint.

rule: Tiempo y duración: el sujeto es it (It takes...).
prompt: Say it again with a subject: Takes about twenty minutes to run.
model: It takes about twenty minutes to run.

rule: El posesivo va antes del sustantivo: my, nunca "of me".
prompt: The first object of me is my wedding ring.
model: My first object is my wedding ring.
wrong: The first object of me is my wedding ring.

rule: El posesivo va antes del sustantivo: my laptop.
prompt: The laptop of me is very slow.
model: My laptop is very slow.
wrong: The laptop of me is very slow.

rule: Sin sustantivo después: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs.
prompt: This laptop isn't the company's. It's ___. (my / mine)
model: This laptop isn't the company's. It's mine.

rule: La única forma con of: a friend of mine / of yours.
prompt: Lucía is a friend of me.
model: Lucía is a friend of mine.
wrong: Lucía is a friend of me.

rule: Ropa y accesorios propios: posesivo, no artículo.
prompt: I always wear the watch at work.
model: I always wear my watch at work.
wrong: I always wear the watch at work.

rule: Uno al otro: each other.
prompt: We support us in the difficult moments.
model: We support each other in difficult moments.
wrong: We support us in the difficult moments.

rule: Sin sustantivo después: mine.
prompt: Answer with mine: Is this branch yours?
model: Yes, this branch is mine.

rule: Cosas, planetas, apps y animales: its.
prompt: Saturn is famous for ___ rings. (his / its)
model: Saturn is famous for its rings.

rule: El posesivo depende del dueño: ella = her.
prompt: My wife wears ___ wedding ring every day. (his / her)
model: My wife wears her wedding ring every day.

rule: El dueño es un hombre: his.
prompt: Martín forgot to update ___ test data. (his / her / its)
model: Martín forgot to update his test data.

rule: Una cosa (la API): its.
prompt: The API changed ___ response format. (his / its / their)
model: The API changed its response format.

rule: Varios dueños: their (antes del sustantivo).
prompt: The developers pushed ___ changes on Friday. (his / their / theirs)
model: The developers pushed their changes on Friday.

rule: Persona sin género conocido: their en singular.
prompt: Each user can change ___ password. (his / their)
model: Each user can change their password.

rule: El dueño manda: tu hija = her.
prompt: My daughter loves his Riolu plush.
model: My daughter loves her Riolu plush.
wrong: My daughter loves his Riolu plush.

rule: Una cosa: its.
prompt: Describe the app: The app lost the session after the update. (use its)
model: The app lost its session after the update.

rule: it's = it is. its = de eso.
prompt: ___ a Pokémon named Riolu. (Its / It's)
model: It's a Pokémon named Riolu.

rule: Posesivo de una cosa: its, sin apóstrofo.
prompt: The service lost ___ connection to the database. (its / it's)
model: The service lost its connection to the database.

rule: It's = it has (it has been).
prompt: ___ been flaky since the last deploy. (Its / It's)
model: It's been flaky since the last deploy.

rule: Posesivo: its. Probá el truco: "because of it is documentation" no tiene sentido.
prompt: I like this framework because of ___ documentation. (its / it's)
model: I like this framework because of its documentation.

rule: you're = you are. your = tu.
prompt: ___ right, ___ fix works. (Your / You're)
model: You're right, your fix works.

rule: whose = de quién. who's = who is.
prompt: ___ PR broke the build? (Whose / Who's)
model: Whose PR broke the build?

rule: Dueño + 's + cosa: my daughter's plush.
prompt: Say it with 's: The plush of my daughter is a Pokémon.
model: My daughter's plush is a Pokémon.

rule: Dueño + 's + cosa: my father's watch.
prompt: Say it with 's: The watch of my father is very old.
model: My father's watch is very old.

rule: Nombre propio + 's: Enzo's PR.
prompt: Say it with 's: The pull request of Enzo is ready.
model: Enzo's pull request is ready.

rule: De quién es algo: belongs to o 's. from = origen.
prompt: This plush is from my daughter. (quiero decir que es de ella)
model: This plush belongs to my daughter.
wrong: This plush is from my daughter.

rule: Plural con -s: solo apóstrofo (developers').
prompt: Write it with an apostrophe: the comments of the developers were useful.
model: The developers' comments were useful.

rule: Plural irregular (sin -s): + 's.
prompt: Say it with 's: The toys of the children are everywhere.
model: The children's toys are everywhere.

rule: Como sujeto va I, y al final.
prompt: Me and my team automated the regression suite.
model: My team and I automated the regression suite.
wrong: Me and my team automated the regression suite.

rule: Después de preposición: me, him, her, us, them.
prompt: Between you and ___, the deadline isn't realistic. (I / me)
model: Between you and me, the deadline isn't realistic.

rule: Objeto: us.
prompt: The QA lead asked ___ for a report. (we / us)
model: The QA lead asked us for a report.

rule: Sujeto y objeto son la misma persona: myself.
prompt: I taught ___ Playwright. (me / myself)
model: I taught myself Playwright.

rule: Sujeto it + verbo con -s: it has.
prompt: Its have a little planet in it.
model: It has a little planet in it.
wrong: Its have a little planet in it.

rule: El verbo concuerda con the test (= it): covers.
prompt: The test that cover the login is failing.
model: The test that covers the login is failing.
wrong: The test that cover the login is failing.

rule: La -s va solo con he / she / it.
prompt: We really likes Lego and Pokémon.
model: We really like Lego and Pokémon.
wrong: We really likes Lego and Pokémon.

rule: Pregunta indirecta: sujeto + verbo, sin invertir.
prompt: I don't know what is the problem.
model: I don't know what the problem is.
wrong: I don't know what is the problem.

rule: Dentro de otra frase: sujeto + verbo (every moment is).
prompt: It shows how important is every moment.
model: It shows how important every moment is.
wrong: It shows how important is every moment.

rule: Usá el sujeto it y el posesivo its (sin apóstrofo).
prompt: Tell me about your watch in one sentence. Use It and its.
model: It's a nice watch, and its face has a small Saturn.

rule: Como sujeto: My team and I...
prompt: Tell me something your team did. Start with My team and I.
model: My team and I automated the whole regression suite.
